preprocessor.detail: AudioToMelSpectrogramPreprocessor: 16 kHz, 128 mels, n_fft 512, win 0.025 s, hop 0.01 s, hann, per_feature, dither 1e-5. Section is identical to nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.

safetensors_metadata.detail: header-only floating dtype distribution; no tensor payloads downloaded

dtype.evidence: config.dtype=float32; safetensors header F32=699 / I64=24, identical distribution to v3. .nemo model_weights.ckpt is the F32 source; converted GGUF is orukeet-F32.gguf.

upstream_benchmarks.notes: NeMo greedy-batch TDT, FP32 weights + BF16 CUDA autocast, publisher's pinned normalizer. Parakeet v3 = 1.53 on the same pipeline. Acceptance dataset.
v3 = 3.14. CAUTION: the r3 final adaptation trained on 2,939 LibriSpeech test-other recordings and used test-other for checkpoint selection, so this split is not held out.
Pooled (errors / reference words), not averaged; v3 = 11.01 on the same pipeline. Per-language table in docs/current-checkpoint-benchmarks.md on the repo.

reference_rationale: Orukeet is a weights-only fine-tune of nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 (model_config.yaml encoder/decoder/joint/preprocessor/decoding sections and the SentencePiece tokenizer are byte-for-byte those of v3). The publisher's benchmark numbers are produced with NeMo (nemo_toolkit[asr] 3.0.0, ASRModel.restore_from on orukeet-v0.1.0.nemo, greedy-batch TDT), so NeMo on the .nemo archive is the oracle, same as the v3 port. The repo also ships a transformers ParakeetForTDT export, a sherpa-onnx INT8 export, Core ML bundles and a 'native' NeMo-Speech.cpp GGUF; those are downstream exports with their own validation, not the reference. The publisher also ships a transcribe.cpp Q8_0 GGUF built with our own convert-parakeet.py at 585b98f7 plus a 20-line profile patch; that file is a cross-check, not an input.
known_risks: Weights-only fine-tune of v3: architecture, hyperparameters, tokenizer and frontend are identical, so src/arch/parakeet needs no changes. The only converter change is a VARIANT_PROFILES entry (slug 'orukeet' from --repo-id oruk/orukeet). Any Stage 4 tensor drift beyond the v3 tolerances is therefore a converter or reference-dump problem, not a runtime one.
Tokenizer: SentencePiece BPE 8192 + blank. tokenizer.model / tokenizer.vocab / vocab.txt inside the .nemo are byte-identical (SHA-256) to nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3. No tokenizer work.

12,288 of the 24,576 encoder depthwise-conv taps (9-tap, 1024 ch x 24 layers) are frozen fitted Gabor values rather than trained weights. They are stored as ordinary F32 conv weights, so no runtime support is needed, but quantization of conv_dw tensors could move these taps more than trained ones would; the Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M quant WER read in Stage 5/7 is the check.

Checkpoint selection and the final 168-step adaptation used LibriSpeech test-other, so test-other is contaminated. test-clean (the acceptance dataset) was not used for training per the card, but treat the publisher's test-other number as non-held-out and do not use test-other as a gate.

Publisher's own 120-clip FLEURS check with our runtime (transcribe-cpp/validation.json) shows Q8_0 worse than stock v3 on de (4.07 vs 3.56), fr (4.50 vs 4.07) and uk (11.60 vs 9.40) and better on en/es/ru. The card's '61 of 74 splits' claim is on their NeMo pipeline; our full FLEURS Q8_0 sweep decides what the model card says.

License is CC-BY-SA-4.0 (ShareAlike), unlike the CC-BY-4.0 of every other parakeet variant we ship. The HF card YAML, catalog record and GGUF general.license must carry cc-by-sa-4.0 and retain the NVIDIA attribution from NOTICE.md.

Publisher reports four sub-block tensor probes exceeding strict tolerances at sequence boundaries (attributed to padding-path differences) while standard probes pass v3 tolerances. Unverified; Stage 4 validate.py against a NeMo dump settles it.
The .nemo is 2.5 GB; use the converter's direct-archive path (prefer_direct_load) to avoid NeMo's extract-to-tmp doubling disk use. Spillover dir is /Volumes/port/models/transcribe.cpp/orukeet.
Multilingual SentencePiece vocab (8192 + blank). Some scripts (Cyrillic, Greek) have higher byte-fallback rates; tokenizer round-trip tests should cover non-Latin samples, not just English.

Long-form audio: v3 model card recommends chunking >35 s clips; the C++ port handles long audio via internal chunking. Boundary handling differs from NeMo's chunked decoder; transcripts can drift at chunk edges if overlap is wrong.
